<!--
  design-system — the overview of the project's design system: its foundations and tokens, its
  component index, the interaction patterns it composes, and how it is governed. Text-first and tool-neutral.
  Lives at: `design/design-system.md` — a singleton, one per design wiki.
  Authorship: curated. SLO: 180d, AND stale whenever any page `realizes:` names is updated after this one —
    either trigger fires. The timer stays alongside the edge: the system can drift from what shipped even though
    the feature it realizes has not changed.
  Owner: fixed to `design`, do not substitute.
  Discipline: the page is the map and the governance, not a token dump — a token group's values live
    in its catalog or in the design-tool library the catalog mirrors, and a component's spec on its
    `ui-component` page; a design-tool library is linked, never copied. Code that realizes the system
    cites this page (`@realizes design:design-system`); the page never links code.
  Columns: Voice and tone — Situation | Tone; Decisions — Decision | State | Decided; Open questions — Question | Owner | Resume condition.
  Required: `## Voice and tone`.
  Extra frontmatter: `realizes` is REQUIRED — what the system as a whole serves. A design system
    serves the product generally rather than one module, so its `realizes:` is exactly one entry, the
    product base `[[product:app-base]]`; the fixed-target rule is in [[_authoring:wiki-page-types]].
    Declaring it is what gives the page a build state of its own — see [[_authoring:wiki-fact-placement#realization-membership]]
    for what makes a page an entry and what a code citation naming it grounds. The system spans all platforms
    (foundations/tokens brand-shared; component realizations may differ per platform, the system stays
    one); a per-platform or per-OS design system is an anti-pattern unless the platforms are different brands.
    `icon-catalog` (OPTIONAL) — [[design:catalogs/<icon-set>]], the `catalog` page in `design` that
    lists the icon names a sitemap's Icon column resolves against; delete the line when the product
    has no icon set. The catalog names its code column in its own `code-column:` when that is not `Code`.
    `invalidates` (OPTIONAL) — dash-list of [[<domain>:<path>]] naming the live pages this decision
    makes partly stale; update each in the same change. Targets must be living pages — a record is
    superseded whole via `superseded-by` instead.
  Disposition: keep every header; "None." when empty.
  Substitute: {{TITLE}} {{DATE}} {{CONFIDENCE}} {{ORIGINATION}}.
-->

## Foundations / tokens
<!-- The foundations every component draws on: color, typography, spacing, elevation, motion, radius,
     the layout grid and its breakpoints, iconography, imagery. For each, its intent — the grid's columns,
     gutters and margins per breakpoint on one base unit; motion's shared easing and duration and its
     reduced-motion behavior; icons named by meaning, with accessible names, and the icons reserved for
     common actions — the icon set itself is the catalog the `icon-catalog:` field names. Summarize the scales inline, OR — preferred when a token set is governed and
     referenced across pages — link a design-homed `catalog` page per token group
     (`catalogs/<token-group>.md`, e.g. `catalogs/color.md`; the shared `catalog` template fits this). Each token group's values have one canonical home: its catalog (`origination: originate`), or the design-tool library the catalog mirrors (`origination: mirror`, recording the values with the library's URL, or the project path of the token files under `tokens/` in the project's design directory (`design.path`)). Token files outside the design directory's `tokens/`, and code, realize the system and take their values from that home.
     This section is the index and the intent. -->

## Component index
<!-- The components in the system, as links to their `ui-component` pages
     ([[design:components/<slug>]]). Group by category when the set grows. Name each by its structure,
     not the context it first appeared in ("card", not "product card"). A component's status and its
     composition and usage (what it is made of, where it is used) live on its page — link, do not repeat
     them here. The index lists every component except one under an application, a top-level module
     whose `product-module` page declares `kind: application`, including one under that application's
     areas or its own `_shared`. Such a component stays local to its application until a second
     application needs it; it then moves out of the application and joins the index. The index lists a
     component at the top level, under a library or the top-level `_shared`, or under a module that
     declares no `kind`. -->

## Interaction patterns
<!-- The recurring compositions of components the system standardizes, each solving one interaction
     problem (forms, empty states, data tables). Each links the components it composes and names the
     content variations it is tested against — one item and many, a first-time user, short and very
     long text, extra permissions. How a page arranges its regions, the application shell included, is
     a layout pattern ([[design:layout-patterns/<slug>]]), and one reusable part's anatomy and states
     are a component's, not a pattern's. -->

## Governance & contribution
<!-- How the system evolves: its makers (who create, maintain and govern it), its users (the teams
     applying it), and who approves a change. How a component/token is modified, added (only once more
     than one application needs it) or removed (deprecated first, naming its replacement); the review it
     needs; how it is versioned; and where changes are announced (the changelog and roadmap, linked).
     The rules that keep the system coherent. -->
